Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 100, verse 1–5:

There is disagreement concerning al-ʿādiyāt, al-mūriyāt and al-mughīrāt: is it intended that they refer to horses or to camels? And on the view that they are horses, there is disagreement whether it means the horses of the fighters in the cause of God, or horses in general? And on the view that they are camels, there is disagreement whether it means the camels of the Battle of Badr, or the camels of the fighters in general, or the camels of the pilgrims, or camels in general?

The meaning of al-ʿādiyāt is those that run (taʿdū) in their going. Al-ḍabḥ (the snorting) is a loud vocalization at the time of intense running, and it is not neighing (ṣahīl). It is a verbal noun in the accusative, on the assumption "they snort a snorting" (yaḍbaḥna ḍabḥan), or it is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), its assumed sense being: "the runners while snorting."

Al-mūriyāt is derived from your saying awraytu al-nār, when you kindle the fire. Al-qadḥ (striking) is the striking of stones so that a spark of fire comes out of them. This happens when the horses' or camels' hooves strike the ground. The grammatical case (iʿrāb) of qadḥan is like that of ḍabḥan.

Al-mughīrāt is derived from your saying aghārat al-khayl, when the horses went out to raid the enemies. Ṣubḥan is an adverb of time, because the habit of raiders is, for the most part, to set out in the morning.

﴿Then they raise thereby a cloud of dust﴾. This sentence is coordinated with al-ʿādiyāt and what follows it, because it is assumed to be "in what runs". Al-naqʿ is the dust. The pronoun in the genitive refers to the time mentioned, which is the morning, so the bāʾ is for time. Or it refers to what the meaning requires, so the bāʾ is also for time. Or it refers to the running (al-ʿadw), which is the verbal noun implied by al-ʿādiyāt, so the bāʾ is causal.

Atharna means ḥarrakna (they stirred), and the subject pronoun refers to the camels or the horses, meaning they stir up the dust as they move.

﴿And thereby penetrate into the midst of a company﴾. The meaning of wasaṭna is tawassaṭna (they penetrated into the midst). As for jamʿan, there is disagreement whether it means a company of people, or al-Muzdalifa, because its name is Jamʿ. The pronoun in the genitive refers to the time, or to the place, or to the running, or to the dust.

﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord﴾. This is the response to the oath. Al-kanūd (ٱلْكَنُود) means the one who denies the blessing. The meaning is: indeed mankind is ungrateful for his Lord's blessing. "Mankind" (al-insān) is a genus. It was said that al-kanūd means the disobedient one. Some of the Sufis (al-ṣūfiyya) said that al-kanūd is the one who worships Allah in exchange for a reward.

﴿And indeed he is a witness to that﴾. The pronoun refers to mankind, meaning that he is a witness against himself through his ingratitude. It was also said that the pronoun refers to Allah, Exalted is He, with the meaning of a warning. The first view is more preferable, because the pronoun that follows refers to mankind by agreement, so the discourse proceeds in one consistent manner.

﴿And indeed he is intensely devoted to wealth﴾. Here al-khayr (ٱلْخَيْر) means wealth, as in His saying: ﴿if he leaves behind wealth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 180]. The meaning is that mankind is intensely attached to wealth, so this is a rebuke of his love for it and his greed for it. It was said that al-shadīd (ٱلشَّدِيد) means the stingy one. According to this view, the meaning is that he is stingy because of his love for wealth. The first view is more apparent.

﴿When what is in the graves is scattered﴾. That is, it is searched out at that time, an expression for resurrection.

﴿And what is in the breasts is brought out﴾. That is, what is in the scrolls is gathered and made manifest, or its good is distinguished from its evil.

﴿Indeed their Lord, concerning them, on that Day, is All-Aware﴾. The pronouns in "their Lord" (rabbahum) and "concerning them" (bihim) refer to mankind, because the word is intended as a genus. In this sentence there are two views. The first: this sentence is the object governed by "Does he not know" (a-fa-lā yaʿlam), so the original form would have been with an opening hamza-less "inna" (an), but it was made "inna" with a kasra because of the lām in its predicate. The second: this sentence is a new, independent statement, and the object governed by "Does he not know" is omitted, and the subject is a pronoun referring to mankind. The implied meaning is: "Does mankind not know his condition and what will come from him when what is in the graves is scattered?" This is what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya also said: "In my view it is possible that the subject of 'Does he not know' is a pronoun referring to Allah, and the object is omitted, and the meaning is: 'Does Allah not know the deeds of mankind when what is in the graves is scattered?' Then he resumed with His saying: ﴿Indeed their Lord, concerning them, on that Day, is All-Aware﴾, as an emphasis or as an explanation of the preceding meaning." According to this interpretation, the element governing "when is scattered" (idhā buʿthira) is "Does he not know," and the element governing it according to the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya is the omitted object. Here "idhā" is temporal, meaning "when" and "at the time," and not conditional. The element governing "on that Day" (yawma'idhin) is "All-Aware" (khabīr). Allah specified that time for the Day of Resurrection because it is the Day of Recompense, with the intent of warning, even though Allah is All-Aware in an absolute sense.

The first: this sentence is the object governed by "Does he not know" (a-fa-lā yaʿlam), so the original form would have been with an opening hamza-less "inna" (an), but it was made "inna" with a kasra because of the lām in its predicate. The second: this sentence is a new, independent statement, and the object governed by "Does he not know" is omitted, and the subject is a pronoun referring to mankind. The implied meaning is: "Does mankind not know his condition and what will come from him when what is in the graves is scattered?" This is what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya also said: "In my view it is possible that the subject of 'Does he not know' is a pronoun referring to Allah, and the object is omitted, and the meaning is: 'Does Allah not know the deeds of mankind when what is in the graves is scattered?' Then he resumed with His saying: ﴿Indeed their Lord, concerning them, on that Day, is All-Aware﴾, as an emphasis or as an explanation of the preceding meaning." According to this interpretation, the element governing "when is scattered" (idhā buʿthira) is "Does he not know," and the element governing it according to the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya is the omitted object. Here "idhā" is temporal, meaning "when" and "at the time," and not conditional. The element governing "on that Day" (yawma'idhin) is "All-Aware" (khabīr). Allah specified that time for the Day of Resurrection because it is the Day of Recompense, with the intent of warning, even though Allah is All-Aware in an absolute sense.

﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord﴾. This is the response to the oath. Al-kanūd (ٱلْكَنُود) means the one who denies the blessing. The meaning is: indeed mankind is ungrateful for his Lord's blessing. "Mankind" (al-insān) is a genus. It was said that al-kanūd means the disobedient one. Some of the Sufis (al-ṣūfiyya) said that al-kanūd is the one who worships Allah in exchange for a reward.

﴿And indeed he is a witness to that﴾. The pronoun refers to mankind, meaning that he is a witness against himself through his ingratitude. It was also said that the pronoun refers to Allah, Exalted is He, with the meaning of a warning. The first view is more preferable, because the pronoun that follows refers to mankind by agreement, so the discourse proceeds in one consistent manner.

﴿And indeed he is intensely devoted to wealth﴾. Here al-khayr (ٱلْخَيْر) means wealth, as in His saying: ﴿if he leaves behind wealth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 180]. The meaning is that mankind is intensely attached to wealth, so this is a rebuke of his love for it and his greed for it. It was said that al-shadīd (ٱلشَّدِيد) means the stingy one. According to this view, the meaning is that he is stingy because of his love for wealth. The first view is more apparent.

﴿When what is in the graves is scattered﴾. That is, it is searched out at that time, an expression for resurrection.

﴿And what is in the breasts is brought out﴾. That is, what is in the scrolls is gathered and made manifest, or its good is distinguished from its evil.
